📈 Timeline
Recorded servo tracks draw as a clean line — click ON the line to add a control point (it snaps to the curve), then drag it to reshape (nearby motion follows — see “Smooth drag”) · select a control point to reveal its two handle arms; drag a handle to bend the curve on that side (handle height = slope, distance = reach — Photoshop-style) · double-click-drag a dot to move just that one · right-click a dot to delete it (or Delete/Backspace, or 🗑) · “All points” shows the raw captured dots · + Action adds an action at the yellow cursor (or click the Actions lane); drag its diamond to move it in time, click to edit, right-click to delete — two actions on the same spot auto-nudge 5 ms apart · Shift-click two control points (no other control point between) for an easing pair · drag the yellow handle to scrub · red ✕ deletes a whole track · ✂ Trim start removes leading empty space; Length sets the clip's total time — raise it to add time at the end (each servo holds its pose out to the new end; drag those end points to animate) · Ctrl+scroll zooms at the pointer, ⤢ Fit fits · Overlay stacks every track into one lane in different colors to line curves up (dots/handles/add all still work); Normalize (on by default) scales each track to its own travel so same-joystick channels sit on top of each other — uncheck it for actual µs on one shared scale · click a track name on the left to focus it: it's highlighted, the rest fade, and new points go to it (great when tracks overlap); click it again to unfocus · ↶ Undo (Ctrl+Z) reverts the last edits (up to 50) · 〰 Smooth lightly smooths the FOCUSED channel's curve — click again for more (focus a track or select a dot on it first) · ⬇ Script exports the clip as Maestro script source (peaks/direction changes only, fits the Maestro's 8 KB script memory) — paste into Control Center's Script tab and trigger it with the "Run a script" action.

Logical Buttons

Matrix-channel logical buttons 15 extra buttons on matrix CH7, not on the transmitter graphic

Mix a transmitter logical switch (or any spare source) onto the matrix channel, then set the value it outputs below. When the matrix channel reaches that value (±10), the logical button fires — with the same per-mode, multi-tap actions as the physical buttons. Switch the mode tabs to map different actions per mode; Configure actions opens the standard editor. Leave the trigger blank to disable a slot.

Transmitter

Model which physical transmitter you're using

The model determines which SVG is displayed, which controls appear in calibration, and the default channel assignments for each control. Calibration still overrides per-control channels individually, so a custom TX mixer setup still works — the model just provides sensible starting points.

X20 hardware options

Check this if your X20 has the optional 3-axis gimbal upgrade — adds the J5 (left-stick twist) / J6 (right-stick twist) axes and the two stick-click momentary buttons (matrix slots 19 / 20) to the axes table, assignment list, and calibration walk. Leave unchecked on a standard 2-axis X20.

WCB Network

Remote WCBs should run firmware 6.2.0 or newer — readable HCR/Maestro verbs, the mesh WCB Status panel, per-board names, and Via WCB relaying all need it. Check a board with ?version.

Profiles — dev / in-droid credential sets

Save the current network credentials as a named profile (e.g. Dev, In-droid), then select one to load it — same functional config, different mesh identity. Stored in the NaviCore config (travels with the droid + cloud backups/exports; includes the password) — Save the config to store profile edits. WCB Network changes only apply over Direct USB, so to switch the droid's mesh: flip to the target profile, connect over USB, then Save.

When a New Peer Is Detected

Optionally run action(s) when a new WCB board joins the mesh. Fires once per board, after an 8 s boot grace so your existing fleet doesn't trigger it.
Triggered when a WCB advertises itself and NaviCore auto-joins it — you don't need to pre-list boards in Quantity.

WCB Send (Test)

(0 = broadcast)
Fires a one-off WCB command without saving. Maestro/Serial testing via terminal or Shift+Click on configured buttons.

Audio Devices

Every sound device the droid can reach, in one place. Each destination is global — an action of that type carries only the command, never a destination, so this is set once and saved to the board. A device you don't have costs nothing left alone.

HCR Vocalizer

All HCR actions route through this destination.

MP3 Trigger

All MP3 Trigger actions route here. Serial = MP3 Trigger wired to this controller's S3/S4/S5. WCB = wired to a WCB (configured there with ?MP3,S<port>). A v2 Trigger wants that port at 38400.

DFPlayer Mini

All DFPlayer actions route here. Serial = DFPlayer wired to this controller's S3/S4/S5. WCB = wired to a WCB (configured there with ?DFP,S<port>). A DFPlayer's baud is fixed at 9600 by the module. Its volume scale is 0 = silent … 30 = loudest — the inverse of the MP3 Trigger's.

Maestro Locations

How long a remote / via-WCB Maestro "busy" reply stays valid before the "Skip if already running" gate gives up and fires anyway.
Defines where each logical Maestro lives. Buttons/knobs only pick "Maestro 1-8" and don't care about the wiring. Every physical Maestro must have a unique Pololu device # (0-127) set in Maestro Control Center — the value here must match it so only the addressed Maestro responds.
Import a Maestro's saved settings file (📁 button or drag-and-drop the file onto a row) to pull in that Maestro's real per-channel endpoints and names — they drive the passthrough ranges and the timeline editor.

WLED Lighting

One row per WLED. Give it an ID (1-9) — the same id your WLED Lighting actions address with ;L<id>,VERB — then route it to a Local port (a WLED wired to one of this controller's aux serial ports, S3/S4/S5) or a Remote WCB (a WLED hosted on another board; the command is forwarded over ESP-NOW). WLED wants 115200 baud — only S3 (the hardware UART) is reliable that fast; set the port's baud in the Serial Ports tab. A bare ;L,VERB (no id) drives the lowest-id local WLED.

Smoothing Profiles

A smoothing profile sets how much each servo channel eases (its Maestro speed + acceleration limits). A joystick knob picks a profile (in its editor), and a Maestro "Set active easing" switch action can load one — so the same servos can glide or snap on demand. Slide right = more easing (slower / gentler); far left = off (snappy). Enable a Maestro in the Maestro tab first, then add its channels here.

Serial Ports

Port Mesh Baud Label — advertised on the mesh (WDP) Bcast out Bcast in
S3 S1
S4 S2
S5 S3
Maestro — — —
S3 is the hardware UART0 (both boards) so it can exceed 57600 (up to 115200); S4/S5 are bit-banged SoftwareSerial (≤57600). One port = one device = one baud (HCR-local / MP3-local / Serial actions). On NaviCore v2 they're silkscreen Serial 1/2/3; on WCB 3.2 they map to its Serial 3/4/5 headers. Maestro = local Pololu Maestro bus (up to 115200).

Mesh is how the rest of the network addresses each port: from any WCB, ;w20,;s2<cmd> writes <cmd> out the port shown as S2 — always available, no setting needed. Bcast out writes mesh broadcasts out that port; Bcast in broadcasts lines read from it to the whole mesh. Both are off by default, and a port an HCR / MP3 / WLED is routed to is skipped either way (its driver owns the wire). Label rides the WDP advert so WCBs + the Wizard show what's attached — blank = auto (the Maestro shows "Maestro"; the aux ports show HCR/MP3/WLED when a dest routes there). Reboot or re-save to apply.

Board / PCB

Selects the GPIO pin map for your hardware. Save, then reboot the board for a change to take effect — pins are assigned at boot. Default: NaviCore v2.

Hold a button this long to fire its Long press tier

Switch Settle

ms
A switch must rest this long before its actions fire. Stops a 3‑position switch from firing the middle position on its way from one end to the other. 0 = fire immediately.

Telemetry Rate

5 Hz
Live channel-monitor rate (rc_ch). Higher is smoother; lower frees mesh airtime.

SBUS Output

Off by default. Enable only if you daisy-chain a downstream SBUS device — leaving it off saves the per-frame CPU of re-transmitting. Applies on Save (no reboot).

Mode Report — mode-select position → a WCB

Off by default. Sends a command to the target WCB carrying the mode-select position on every switch change and every 60 s. Command uses {mode} → the position (1/2/3); a non-blank per-mode override replaces it for that position (blank = send nothing for that mode). The default ;V,MODE,{mode} sets the target WCB's MODE variable to the position — the ; prefix keeps it targeted (a command with no ; prefix is instead re-broadcast out every WCB's serial ports mesh-wide). Applies on Save.

Mesh Stats — ESP-NOW delivery counters

optional — leave blank to collect without shipping
Off by default. The counters always run — they start at boot and accumulate until the board reboots, whatever this is set to. Turning this on tells the tool this droid uses them, so WCB Status shows the per-board numbers from the moment you connect (already covering everything since boot, not just since you looked).

Report to WCB is optional. Blank = collect and display here only. Set it and every 30 s this board also sends one command to that WCB — ?STATS,RPT,<from>,<sent>,<ackd>,<retries>,<failed>,<unguaranteed>,<bcast>,<recv> — which it stores and lists under ?STATS in a Reported by Other Nodes section, so one board can collect the whole fleet. These are this board's own numbers only; every other node reports its own the same way. Because it is a ? command it is handled locally there and is never re-broadcast or written to its serial ports. Those stored rows are RAM-only and clear on that board's reboot. Shipping requires WCB firmware with ?STATS,RPT. Applies on Save.
live diagnostics — also shown under WCB Status

Flashes the latest NaviCore firmware to a WCB v3.2 (ESP32-S3) board. Pulls the binary from github.com/greghulette/NaviCore/firmware. Your saved configuration (NVS) is preserved unless the partition layout changed.
To enter bootloader mode: hold BOOT, tap RST, release BOOT. Then click one of the buttons below. Chrome will ask which USB port to use.
Idle.
Update Firmware — keeps your saved config intact. Use this for routine firmware updates.
Full Wipe & Flash — factory-fresh push. Erases NVS and OTA data along with the firmware. Use for the very first flash on a new board, or to recover from corruption / bad config. You will lose all saved settings.
